question: A 28-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of lower extremity numbness, weakness, and urinary incontinence. She has not had any trauma. Neurologic examination shows bilateral lower extremity weakness. Stroking the lateral side of the sole of the foot from the heel to the base of the small toe and medially to the base of the big toe elicits dorsiflexion of the big toe and fanning of the other toes. Further examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following additional findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lower extremity numbness, weakness, and urinary incontinence" -> "Possible spinal cord lesion" -> "Bilateral lower extremity weakness" -> "Upper motor neuron involvement" -> "Spasticity" -> "Positive Babinski sign" -> "Spasticity" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Stroking lateral side of the sole elicits dorsiflexion of the big toe and fanning of other toes" -> "Positive Babinski sign" -> "Upper motor neuron lesion" -> "Spasticity" -> "Hyperreflexia" -> "Spasticity" -> 90%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with lower extremity weakness and positive Babinski sign indicates upper motor neuron involvement, suggesting spasticity. Additional findings are likely to include spasticity and hyperreflexia, supporting the presence of upper motor neuron lesions.
analysis: The patient's presentation with lower extremity weakness, positive Babinski sign, and upper motor neuron involvement suggests a likely diagnosis of spinal cord pathology. The presence of spasticity and hyperreflexia further supports this, indicating upper motor neuron lesions. Given this context, the most likely additional finding in this patient would be spasticity.
